comment: Known differences between two canonical graph dumps (jets/rulesbench/graphdump), read by rules_bench_diff and embedded in it. A difference is unclassified unless an entry matches. Fields and pair kinds: README.md beside this file. Each entry names where the difference is recorded: a section of jets/jetrules/rete/README.md or a register entry of projects/rules_benchmark.

entries.description: The line is the same on both sides up to the label of a minted node, under a one-to-one correspondence of labels: the node is on both sides and was renamed because its neighbourhood within three hops differs. What differs is in its own lines, which are classified on their own.

refs: jets/jetrules/rete/README.md, The Go and C++ engines are independently maintained and they disagree, item 3
entries.description: The Go engine quantises a double literal to 15 bits of mantissa (ResourceManager.NewDoubleLiteral); C++ keeps it. The two values are equal once both are quantised.

The Go engine names a lookup result jets:lookup:<key> (jets:lookup:multi:<key> for a multi-lookup), without the table, so two tables looked up with the same key share one subject, which carries both tables' columns and both rows' jets:row_id (LookupTableSqlite3.Lookup, jets/jetrules/rete/lookup_table_sqlite3.go). C++ names it jets:<table>:<key> (LookupTable::lookup_internal, jets/rete/lookup_sql_helper.cc), one subject per table. In the dump: one minted node on Go where C++ has one per table.

A multi-lookup's cache triple: Go writes (jets:cache:<table> jets:lookup_multi_rows <subject>) (LookupTableSqlite3.MultiLookup), C++ (<table> jets:lookup_row <subject>) (LookupTable::lookup_internal), which the dump renames jets:cache:<table>. Bookkeeping: the 26 uses of jets:lookup_row and jets:lookup_multi_rows in the four workspaces' rule files (counted 2026-10-20) all read them as (?x jets:lookup_… ?y), and none names a cache resource.
entries.subject: jets:cache:.*

refs: jets/jetrules/rete/README.md, The Go and C++ engines are independently maintained and they disagree, item 3
entries.description: A double the Go engine computed from quantised literals: within 2^-12 (about 2.4e-4) of the C++ value, relative to the larger. One quantum is 2^-15 relative; the tolerance allows a few quanta through arithmetic. Weaker evidence than go-double-literal-quantised: a genuine difference this small would be classified here too.

Text + double writes the number differently: Go formats it with %v, the shortest form (Node.ADD, jets/jetrules/rdf/ast_math_operators.go), and C++ with std::to_string, six decimals (AddVisitor, jets/rete/expr_op_arithmetics.h). "rate: 991" on Go is "rate: 991.000000" on C++. Matched when the texts are equal once their numbers are written alike.

refs: jets/jetrules/rete/README.md, Operator names are not registered anywhere but the two factories (apply_regex)
entries.description: literal_regex returns the whole match, or an empty string on no match, on Go (ApplyRegexOp.Eval), and capture group 1, or null on no match, on C++ (RegexVisitor). usi_ws z004 (^(\d\d\d) on a rendering provider zip): a zip that does not start with three digits gives an empty hc_usi:claimZip3 on Go and none on C++.

literal_regex as above, on walrus_ws's name-splitting rules (merge_claim_header_and_details_main.jr): on Go pt_fname keeps the comma and the space (", John") and pt_lname the comma ("Doe,"); on C++ they are the capture groups.
